junction.name: Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street, New York City

claims.text: Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street had 68 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 9 pedestrians injured, 5 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street's own: the city's record places 44 of the 195 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.7 million a year.
37% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading west in 35% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 18% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).
Held up on later years: only people in vehicles hurt and it happened in the daytime in 26% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 15% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).

This corner got turn traffic calming in 2021. Across the city: a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program. Repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.2 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the city's own past installs passed the causal gate), worth $80,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.0 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $698,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Atlantic Avenue, Logan Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 37, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 5.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 37, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 5
Subject: Request for safety review and signal improvements at Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

I am writing to request a safety study at Atlantic Avenue & Logan Street and consideration of low-cost signal fixes on the roads you are responsible for: Atlantic Avenue and Logan Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 136 crashes, including 68 injury crashes. Pedestrians and cyclists are among those hurt: 9 pedestrians injured and 5 cyclists injured, with people killed recorded as 0. This location is identified as a city priority location. The latest recorded safety project here was turn traffic calming in 2021, with no recorded treatment in the current period recorded as false. The yearly cost of the harm, in the U.S. DOT's official values (2024 dollars), is $4.7 million per year.

Please consider, subject to a site check:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent about 0.2 pedestrian injury crashes per year ($80,000 in harm avoided per year). Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.

* reflective backplates on the traffic signals, expected to prevent about 2.0 injury crashes per year ($698,000 in harm avoided per year), pending a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

This corner got turn traffic calming in 2021. Across the city a simple before/after comparison cannot credit a decline to the program because a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the earlier program's effect was not shown. Please consider a different approach as above and advise on next steps for the study.

Thank you for considering these requests.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Sources:
- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 9918 (a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green))
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 1410 (reflective backplates on the traffic signals)
- U.S. DOT Benefit-Cost Analysis Guidance, 2026 Update, Table A-1 (2024 dollars)
- NearMissLens NML-Bench T11: before/after study of the city's own installs (validation/BENCH.md)
- Road owners: the registry's road-inventory layer (see the engineer report's receipts)
